title: Classitis / Over-Modularization
pattern: Fragile decomposition resulting in a high density of tiny, shallow classes or modules that each contain a trivial amount of code but expose separate interfaces.
why_bad: It drastically inflates the overall system complexity by multiplying interfaces and import boilerplate. The mental effort of navigating files and tracing connections between shallow units exceeds the effort of understanding their logic, causing high cognitive load.
detection: A large collection of structs or modules each containing fewer than a few lines of logic (excluding boilerplate) and exposing trivial interfaces.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Autogenerated glue code, protocol buffers, or highly mathematical library modules where operations are inherently split into elemental concepts.
fix: Merge related small, shallow classes into fewer, deeper modules that hide substantial implementation details behind a clean, unified API.
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 4 ("Modules Should Be Deep - Classitis"), pp. 25, 293.
